To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HCV‐RNA levels are a sensitive and specific indicator of liver disease in patients with HCVAb and normal ALT levels, and that the histological picture in HCVAb carriers is almost invariably abnormal.
HCV‐RNA, and not HCVAb or serum ALT levels, is a sensitive and reliable marker of liver disease.
serum HCV-RNA levels are an accurate indicator of the severity of liver disease in patients with HCVAb, and that HCV-RNA-negative patients are likely to have normal liver histology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histological findings of HCV‐RNA and HCVAb in asymptomatic hepatitis carriers.
the clinical significance of HCVAb and the histopathological findings of liver biopsies in patients with HCV infection.
the clinical management of asymptomatic individuals with HCVAb and/or HCV‐RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCV‐RNA positivity in the absence of ALT elevation is an indication for liver biopsy.
the histology of liver disease in asymptomatic carriers of HCV is related to the presence of HCV‐RNA in the serum, and not to HCVAb.
HCV‐RNA positivity is the most sensitive and specific marker for the presence of histological liver damage in HCVAb carriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCV‐RNA positivity correlates with liver disease in asymptomatic HCVAb carriers, and that HCVAb‐RNA negativity is a marker of healthy liver.
the presence of HCV‐RNA in the serum indicates the presence of liver disease and is a good marker for monitoring the response to therapy.
HCV‐RNA testing should be performed in HCVAb carriers who have normal ALT levels, and that liver biopsy should be performed if the HCV‐RNA test is positive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of HCV‐RNA in serum indicates the presence of liver disease, even in the absence of symptoms and/or abnormal serum liver tests.
the presence of HCV‐RNA correlates with histological findings in HCVAb carriers, even if they do not have symptoms of liver disease.
HCV RNA is a more sensitive indicator of liver disease than HCV antibodies.
